To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) MapReduce workloads have a much larger fraction of short jobs than previously reported; 2) MapReduce jobs have a much higher degree of variability than previously assumed; 3) MapReduce work has a much larger fraction (over 40%) of jobs that are query-like than previously assumed; and 4) the MapReduce workloads we observed are more interactive than previously reported.

(1) the new MapReduce workload is driven in part by querylike programming frameworks, (2) MapReduce workloads are more diverse than previously thought, (3) MapReduce jobs are more interactive than expected, (4) the new workload has a higher degree of parallelism than previously thought, and (5) MapReduce work is more data intensive than previously thought.
MapReduce workloads are dominated by short jobs, are driven by interactive analysis, are data-centric, are not uniform in their access patterns, and do not exhibit regular diurnal patterns.
